diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition line 28 gives u(t) in F^m, x(t) in F^N and y(t) in F^p. Hence B:F^m→F^N and A:F^N→F^N meet at the state sum; C:F^N→F^p and D:F^m→F^p meet at the output sum. Every block uses the matrices and directions in that definition.

The two positive inputs to the first circle are Bu and Ax; its output is labelled x′. The integration block is explicitly x0 + integral from t0 to t of its input. At t=t0 it gives x0, and the equation is understood almost everywhere, as stated in the unchanged definition and the new prose. The oriented integral also applies for t<t0; the figure does not impose a new forward-time restriction.

The state output branches downward into A, whose arrow returns upward to the state sum. The input branches before B upward through D into the output sum. Cx and Du therefore add to y without routing Du through the integrator, exactly as in definition line 28.
The original rigorous definition remains unchanged and stands independently of the illustration; the figure supplies neither a new hypothesis nor a proof premise.
